title: Short-video script (TikTok, Reels, Shorts; organic or ad)

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, result, customer reaction, testimonial or before/after that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research; no actor or AI avatar presented as a real customer or employee; no mocked-up product screens. Gaps are written around (pick an angle the confirmed facts fully support); never an invention, never a placeholder in publishable copy.

Limits and format: the script includes a timed beat table, on-screen text, voiceover, shot list, caption and CTA; length fits the platform and use (Reels up to 3 minutes; TikTok in-feed ads 5-60 s); the hook lands within 0-2 s; text is kept out of the bottom ~20% and right edge; hashtags fit the platform (Instagram 5 max; none in non-Spark TikTok ad captions).

Policy: paid, gifted or creator content carries a paid-partnership label or clear #ad; realistic AI-generated voice or visuals are labelled; only licensed audio; no reposted or watermarked footage; no engagement bait; no banned phrases from copy-fundamentals.

anchors.1: Logo, intro, "Hey guys" or a slow establishing shot.
anchors.3: States the topic in time, but the first frame is static or the line is generic.
anchors.5: Payoff or pattern-break first frame plus a spoken line of 10 words or fewer naming the viewer's situation or a confirmed number, mirrored on screen.

anchors.1: Polished TV-ad script or brochure voiceover.
anchors.3: Phone-shot, but the lines sound scripted or salesy.
anchors.5: Indistinguishable from good organic content; talks like a person; format native to the platform.

anchors.1: No timings; talking description instead of visuals; several ideas.
anchors.3: Timed beats in a sensible order, but some beats tell instead of show or carry more than one fact.
anchors.5: Hook, setup, value, proof, CTA with timings; one fact and a new visual per beat; end frame loops or lands cleanly.

anchors.1: Needs crew, actors, a studio or unconfirmed locations; no shot list.
anchors.3: Doable with effort; shot list vague ("some B-roll").
anchors.5: Shot list the owner can film on a phone in one session with confirmed people and places, with framing, action, duration and practical notes.
The viewer's search phrase is spoken, on screen and in the caption's first line.

anchors.1: No captions; key message only in the voiceover; text in unsafe zones.
anchors.3: Captions noted, but on-screen text repeats paragraphs or strays into unsafe zones.
anchors.5: Burned-in captions for every spoken word, short on-screen text per cut that tells the story alone, all inside the safe zone.

anchors.1: Adjectives and claims with no evidence.
anchors.3: Some real details, but the proof beat is vague or missing.
anchors.5: A confirmed number, permitted quote or real result shot carries the proof beat; unmistakably this business.

anchors.3: Clear but generic, or only spoken or only on screen.
anchors.5: One platform-appropriate action, spoken and on screen, matched to awareness level and backed by a real process (someone replies, link exists).

anchors.3: On-topic but not tied to a specific pillar, objection or trigger.
anchors.5: Expresses one positioning element through the viewer's own words and situation.
